newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher after benign U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher after benign U.S. data.

text.p: French shares ended higher after key U.S. economic data showed inflation was restrained.
But turnover remained limited as many investors had stayed on the sidelines awaiting the U.S. figures.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 11.49 points or 0.54 percent at 2,147.12 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,152 from 2,138 on Thursday's close.
* Elf-Aquitaine up 2.8 percent to 405 francs after SGB sold seven million shares. French foreign minister on visit in Bakou, where Elf has 10 percent of Shah Deniz field.
* Over the week, the CAC-40 index lost 17.06 points or 0.79 percent.
* Bouygues up 4.21 percent to 508 francs after announcing telecommunications alliance with STET of Italy.
* Rhone Poulenc down 0.43 percent to 139.50 francs after falling nearly three percent on Thursday following profit warning.

* Rhone-Poulenc's unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said on Thursday its profits would be 10 to 12 percent below forecasts due to a product recall. Rhone-Poulenc said its 1996 net could drop by six to seven percent as a result.
* Alcatel Alsthom up 1.3 percent to 455.60. Company seen winning the bidding for state-electronics group Thomson SA.

* Havas down 3.61 percent at 344.90 on market disappointment over small rise in half year profit. Havas said net income after goodwill amortisation was 413 million francs for the first six months of 1996 against a pro forma 406 million last year.
"The results are not good quality," said one analyst. "There is a decline in operating income and a rise in exceptionals that is going to undermine the 1997 results."
* Bic up 5.41 percent to 740 francs on the back of an 11 percent increase in third quarter sales and a small acquisition in Germany, dealers said.
